en: Ecclesiastes 10

p.src: 1  Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

en: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
u.src: 1  Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

p.src: 2  A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.

en: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
u.src: 2  A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.

p.src: 3  Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.

en: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
u.src: 3  Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.

p.src: 4  If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

en: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
u.src: 4  If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

p.src: 5  There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.

en: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
u.src: 5  There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.

p.src: 6  Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

en: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
u.src: 6  Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

p.src: 7  I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

en: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
u.src: 7  I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

p.src: 8  He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

en: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
u.src: 8  He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

p.src: 9  Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.

en: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.
u.src: 9  Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.

p.src: 10  If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

en: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
u.src: 10  If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

p.src: 11  If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.

en: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
u.src: 11  If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.

p.src: 12  The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.

en: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
u.src: 12  The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.

p.src: 13  The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

en: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
u.src: 13  The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

p.src: 14  A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?

en: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
u.src: 14  A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?

p.src: 15  The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.

en: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
u.src: 15  The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.

p.src: 16  Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!

en: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
u.src: 16  Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!

p.src: 17  Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

en: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
u.src: 17  Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

p.src: 18  By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

en: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
u.src: 18  By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

p.src: 19  A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.

en: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
u.src: 19  A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.

p.src: 20  Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.

en: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
u.src: 20  Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
